en: The Dhāraṇī of the Aspects of Omniscience.
Oṃ! Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!
Thus have I heard:

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain together with a great saṅgha of twelve hundred bhikṣus, headed by many great śrāvakas and others, as well as a retinue of bodhisattvas, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, kings, ministers, and citizens of the countryside.

Then, at that time, the Blessed One— surrounded and honored by the fourfold assembly, and refined by their worship and other offerings— began to speak a Dharma discourse, a sūtra entitled *The Great Vaipulya Following the Bodhisattvas and Upheld by All Buddhas: A Teaching on the Practice of the Samādhi of the Array of Happiness, the Dhāraṇī of the Sphere of the Samādhi of the Array of Vows for Manifesting the Domain of the Bodhisattvas*.
Then, rays of light of various colors issued forth, and by their radiance, this great trichiliocosm was filled with a vast illumination.
[Page 7] Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Ratnavairocana, having seen that great sign and miraculous display,
suddenly rose, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and placed his right knee upon the ground.
Bowing with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was, he said this to the Blessed One:
"It has been a supreme marvel, O Blessed One, that I have attained this. From whence have these rays come? To whom does this power over the sensory domain belong?"
"What will be the cause and condition for this?
The Blessed One said,
"Noble son, there is [a place] in the southeastern direction."

Beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddha-fields, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges from here, there is a world-system named Padmā, adorned with various jewels of diverse virtues, beautified by various jeweled gabled pavilions, trees, flowers, and lotus ponds, where Bodhisattvas bound to only one more birth listen to the Dharma in the presence of the Tathāgata Padmottara.
In that world-system, there is a great Bodhi tree named Indra, made of precious gems.
At its base there is a lotus made of jewels with hundreds of thousands of millions of golden petals.
There, during the first watch of the night, Padmottara, the Arhat and Perfectly Enlightened One, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.
Seated upon that lotus throne, the Bodhisattvas beheld his miraculous displays.

Those bodhisattvas who had come from all the world-systems, having made that offering, remained there. Then, the Tathāgata Padmottara, knowing their dispositions and latent tendencies, for the benefit and happiness of many people and out of compassion for the world, [acted].
For the benefit of gods and humans and for the sake of fulfilling the Mahāyāna, he set in motion the irreversible wheel of Dharma.
The Bodhisattva asked:
"Blessed One, how long will that world-system endure, and for how long will the Tathāgata Padmottara remain, as well as his True Dharma?"
The Blessed One said:
"Noble son, the lifespan of the Tathāgata Padmottara will be thirty intermediate kalpas,
and his True Dharma will remain for ten intermediate kalpas."
The lifespan of those bodhisattvas born there was forty intermediate kalpas.
Furthermore, noble son, that world-system formerly bore the name Candanā;
however, it was not as pure nor filled with pure beings as this world-system is now.

"Noble son, in the world-system Candanā, there was a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Candrottama, who taught the Dharma for twenty intermediate kalpas. At the time of his parinirvāṇa, some of the bodhisattvas departed for other buddha-fields by the power of their vows. As for those bodhisattvas who remained, this thought occurred to them:"

Tonight, during the middle watch, the Tathāgata Candrottama will enter parinirvāṇa, and his True Dharma will remain for ten intermediate kalpas. Who, immediately following the disappearance of the True Dharma, will realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?
Furthermore, at that time, there was a bodhisattva named Gaganamudra who had been prophesied by the Tathāgata Candrottama through his former vow:
"Son of good family, after I have passed into parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain for ten intermediate kalpas;
at the first watch of the night, my True Dharma will disappear."
In that very same night, during the final watch, you shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment;
you shall become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Padmottara.
At that time, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas approached the place where the Tathāgata Candrottama was.
Having approached, they all performed worship of Candrottama with various kinds of bodhisattva-transformations and said this to the Blessed One:
"Venerable Blessed One, we wish to pass these ten intermediate kalpas with our minds focused on cessation.
Then, noble son, the Tathāgata Candrottama addressed the bodhisattva Gaganamudrā, saying this:

"Take up, O son of good family, this entrance into the dhāraṇī-door of the aspects of omniscience, which was taught by all the Tathāgatas, the perfectly awakened ones, of the past and the future, for the Bodhisattvas consecrated to the position of crown prince;
and those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who currently reside in all the world-systems throughout the ten directions, they too teach it."
Those Blessed Buddhas who will appear in the future time will also teach it to the bodhisattvas who have been consecrated as crown princes. Namely:
*jalijalini mahājalini phutke butke saṃmade mahāsaṃmade*.
Devām aṭi caṭi ṭake ṭharaṭharkke amimakasi hili cili tili ruruke mahāruruke,
jaya durjaye jaye jayamati śānte śāntanirghoṣaṇi, amūlaparichinne.
In terrifying the army of Māra,
liberated and completely purified,
fearless and the deliverer from fear.
The bearer of the burden, the tamed one, the supreme among those possessing knowledge and ignorance, the restrainer of adversaries,
and the benefactor of those who speak the Dharma.
This is the word for illuminating the stage of resolute conviction regarding the four foundations of mindfulness of those who speak the Dharma as protection:
*buddhakāśaye*, *amama*, *nimama*,
*avevi*, *arthe*, *arthani*, *stīraṇe*.
In the inclination toward the world, in the application and cultivation,
and in the four noble lineages.
The words that reveal the stage of resolute belief;
when spoken, they are spoken; when maintained, they are maintained.
In the secret, in the auspiciously radiant, in that fruit, in the supreme fruit, in the fruitless, in the blue, in the unliberated, in the liberated,
in the completely liberated, in the protector, in the one who possesses liberation, in the fruit of the void.
"Like one who is unyoked," [said] Ratitula; "the balance, the balance is indeed non-violence."
Having crossed over and not being crossed over in the entire world, you have become a lamp for many beings;
O one who has destroyed the darkness!
Veśāgravate, aphala,
kaphala.
This is the stage of resolute conviction regarding the three things that are to be guarded:
dullness, and this fruit which is neither to be removed nor to be described.
The fruit of the path of certainty,
the ornament for its full attainment,
behold it with joy!
Slightly intoxicated yet not intoxicated,
standing in the posture of the ten-powered one while reciting the mantra for cutting down,
established in the bow.
Sunirghoṣa,
Tīkṣṇamati,
Āloka,
Excessive craving, lack of intelligence,
and striking the Buddhas of the present in the past;
This is the word that illuminates the stage of resolute belief in the four right efforts:
anye manye mane.
Mamane,
vire virate,
śame śamitāvi.
In the peaceful, the liberated, the beyond-sensory, the equal, the perfectly equal,
the exhausted, and the inexhaustible.
Ajiti, Śānte, Samiṣṭhe,
Dhāraṇī-ālokāvabhāse,
Ratnavrate.
To Rasamyavata, to Jñānavata,
and to Meruvata.
In the demonstration of destruction,
in the demonstration of the lamp of the world, this is the word that illuminates the stage of resolute belief regarding the four analytical knowledges. SjDh_5
The eye is the manifestation in appearance and demonstration, and it is the manifestation of the light of knowledge;
it shines forth, transcends the level of all sense faculties,
and is free from all faults.
May all diseases go to destruction;
O Gokāha,
you who possess the splendor of beholding the worlds, [protect us].
This is the word that reveals the stage of resolve regarding the four bases of psychic power:
*Acale buddhe vṛddhapracale,
satva gṛhṇa siddhi*.
The prohibited ones tremble; the supreme ones are fixed in their heads.
Having bestowed the moon and the sun, the immovable ones become immovable, while others are agitated, falling, moving about, spreading forth, approaching, and practicing in this manner.

Kaṃkame, Prabhāvini, Drāme, Nijasā, Grakkrame, Nayane; this is the word that illuminates the stage of resolute belief regarding the powers of the faculties. Puṣpe, Supuṣpe. *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-dharmaparyāya*, Chapter 7.
Drumaparihāra, Abhayarucira, Cekaratka,
May it be inexhaustible;
O Niniṛe, O Mamale, O Pañcaśiśire!

O Cakravajra, this is the word that illuminates the stage of resolute conviction regarding the seven factors of enlightenment— which are known by the world, subsumed by method, and joined with excellent faith. SjDh_8
O you who have attained the meditative absorption of loving-kindness,
who have transcended [the world],
O compassionate one, look upon us with pity!
In the form of joy, endowed with patience, in the wheel-less, in the best,
in the harsh, in the harsh.
In the absence of a root, the root is the means of accomplishment;
this is the word that illuminates the state of resolute belief regarding the four grounds of self-confidence. SjDh_9
Vartte, Cakre, Cakradhare, Varacakre, Vare, Pravare, Hile, Hire,
Dhare, Ārūpāvate.
Just as the tongue is bent back,
just as one moves toward the other shore, and just as one goes toward the destruction of fear, so too is there the removal of falsehood.
The extraction of old age,
the extraction of vigor, the extraction of the path from the peak, the extraction of concentration, the extraction of wisdom, and the extraction of liberation.
The emergence of the knowledge and vision of liberation, the emergence of the stars, the emergence of the moon, the emergence of the sun;
and regarding the fourfold steps of the Tathāgata: it is marvelous, yet not marvelous; perfectly awakened, yet not awakened; awakened here, yet awakened everywhere.
There, the unawakened ones are struck down;
O Arada, O Darada, O Pandala, O Pandala! Therein lies the afflicted one;
O Māṅgagharaṇī, O Pūṭanī, O Saṃprapūṭanī!
O you who have gone beyond all movement,
O destroyer, O binder of destruction,
O cutter!
The piercing of the heart, indeed,
is the best death,
[occurring] at the time of slaying.
Bhare bhare bhunde bhire bhire ruṣare, saraṇe, daraṇe.
O you who set forth,
O you who move,
O you who are swift and excellent!
O Brahmacārin, O Indravani,
O Dhidhirayani!
O beloved of Maheśvara, O my lady, O consort,
O you who reveal the single syllable!
The sun moves as far as the moon; all heroes are inferior heroes; again, those who are born.
Adorned with necklaces and armlets,
O Gandharva,
may we find delight here.
O Bhīrūṇī, O Siddhamatte,
O Vilokamati,
O you who are empowered by the Buddha!
This is the phrase for the manifestation of the inclination toward the ten powers within the gateway of the dhāraṇī.
Immediately upon the Blessed One’s commencement of this entry into the gateway of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience, this trichiliocosm shook in six ways.
By such a radiance, all world-systems in the ten directions appeared clearly, as level as the palm of a hand. Furthermore,
those bodhisattvas dwelling in them who had attained meditative absorptions, dhāraṇīs, and patient endurance— by the power of the Tathāgata—
vanished from their respective buddha-fields and came to this Sahā world-system to Gṛdhrakūṭa.

They approached the presence of the Blessed One, bowed their heads at his feet, performed various kinds of worship, and sat down right there for the purpose of hearing the entrance into the gate of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience.

Transcending all calculation, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, humans, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, and others also gathered there; they beheld that buddha-field Padmā, surrounded by a great multitude of bodhisattvas.

And they behold the Tathāgata. Immediately upon the utterance of this entrance into the gateway of the dhāraṇī by the Blessed One, this dhāraṇī was attained by bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of seventy-two Ganges rivers, [beholding] the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, residing in all world-systems throughout the ten directions.
And they beheld the magnificent arrays of qualities;
struck with wonder, they performed worship to the Buddha and remained there through the power of their meditative concentration.
The Blessed One said:
Noble son, when a bodhisattva cultivates this entrance into the gateways of dhāraṇīs, they attain eighty-four hundred thousand, seventy-two thousand, and sixty thousand dhāraṇīs,
as well as great loving-kindness, compassion, and so forth. Furthermore,
those who hear this dhāraṇī will become non-retrogressive.
Those who write it down shall never be deprived of the vision of the Buddha, the hearing of the true Dharma, and the service of the Saṅgha.
Those who cause it to be written shall never be deprived of unsurpassed parinirvāṇa.
For those who recite it, all their karmic obstructions will go to complete exhaustion.
For those who cultivate it, their five acts of immediate retribution shall be destroyed as non-actions.
Those who uphold it will attain the ten stages beginning with the Joyful (pramuditā).
Those who recite it will attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
And those who explain it in detail to others become Tathāgatas.
Then the Blessed One said this to the Bodhisattva Maitreya:
"Indeed, noble son, it is by the power of this dhāraṇī that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past, future, and present have attained perfect enlightenment.
Long ago, noble son, I received this dhāraṇī from the presence of the Perfectly Enlightened One Kāśyapa."
By the power of this dhāraṇī, perfect enlightenment was attained;
even now it has been retained, recited, and extensively proclaimed by me to others.
Thus indeed, Maitreya, just as the bodhisattva Gaganamudrā obtained, retained, and recited this dhāraṇī from the presence of the Tathāgata Candrottama.

By the power of this dhāraṇī, the bodhisattva Gaganamudrā, on the very night when the True Dharma had vanished during the first watch following the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Candrottama, attained perfect enlightenment during the final watch; he became the Tathāgata named Padmottara in the world-system Padmā.
In the same way, noble son, from my presence you should maintain, recite, and extensively proclaim to others this Drāviḍa mantra-word, the *Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇī*.
By its power, when the lifespan of beings reaches eighty thousand years, there will appear a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Maitreya.
By him, O Maitreya, the position of crown prince has now been received from me.
Just as in the presence of the past Tathāgatas, the Bodhisattvas of the past accepted the position of crown prince.
Then the Blessed One, having surveyed the entire assembly, at that time spoke these mantra-words: namely:

the stage of being tamed, the stage of self-control, the stage of mindfulness, the stage of wisdom, the stage of fearlessness, the stage of analytical knowledge, the stage of non-elevation, the stage of equanimity through the exhaustion of all things, the stage of the exhaustion of birth—*muja vinmujaḥ*.
The son of Mālatī,
Visāgra,
having crossed over the ten stages through his conduct.
Veśalagra,
Śamuśavataḥ, Vimati,
Vimati-yopahira, Regamata, Vasiṣṭhakrama— thus [it is] in Coravate.

In the sacrifice, the mudrās are small; the eyes of wisdom are like bubbles, burning away the sequence [of defilements] along with their faults. Elaya, tilaya, ahusuṭā, amundhamam, arthavati, muruvati—by these, one is devoid of duality.
Akanati, Bakanate, Samake, Visābhaṭe, Iṭe, Iṭabale. Here and there, O Kuruṣa, O Laruṣa; and thus, O Sarvanta, O Sarvantava, Aniruddha, look upon this pillar!
Phala, Bahuphala, Śataphala, and Śiṣṭavate.
The Blessed One also proclaimed to the gods words of resolute conviction concerning dependent origination;
while these were being proclaimed, sixty nayutas of gods attained the vision of the Truths.
That fruit was the supreme fruit.
O Lalaha, O Alaha, O Nilaṃhare,
this fruit has been declared by Vaca;
it is the fruit of self-restraint.
The wheel of the arising and passing away, the wheel of wisdom, and the wheel of perfect nirvana.
The Wheel of the Knower:

through these words of resolute conviction, the minds of ten million gods were set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and they became established therein as non-retrogressive. Look, Mōmate! *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* 12.
O Anumati, O Akumata, O Akumati Cchīdattake,
O Mantasthā, O Deśabala, O Vipravastha, O Īśasthita!
Atimati, Tīkṣṇamati,
and Ālokastejitūṣṇa— by these words of resolute conviction, the minds of sixty-four thousand nāgas were set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
In that very place, they are irreversible and restrained;
they are without radiance, free from pride, and those who are not to be overcome, O Blessed One.
Karaṇyākṣa,
Siddhamati, Samantakṣau,
Alabale, Piṭakaro, Mahābale,
Ojadhara, Dharaṇe, Migalakṣa,
Udākṣa, Kukākṣa, and Viroya.
Virūpamukha, Akṣihasta, Saṃkṣiptabala, Asurodīna, Asuropramardana.

By means of these words of resolute conviction, the minds of twelve koṭis of yakṣas were set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and they became irreversible right there. SjDh_14 Arthe, Pilile, Tinithe, Saṃtīthe.
Katitena nakeme,
nanamaste, ubherabhe.
O joyful one,
O intoxicating one,
O wise one!
O hero,
together with the Śūras, the Dhāraṇīyas, Indra, the gods, and the Nāgas.
Together with yakṣas, asuras, and devas,
the nāgas, the retinue of Nirukti,
and those who delight in etymological analysis.

They have attained mindfulness, wisdom, retinue, and intelligence; they have attained movement and stability along with their retinues; they have practiced beneficial deeds in the past and possess resolute aspiration.
Possessing heroes, possessing long-standing valor, and possessing those who are fearless in the bright fortnight;
O Sealer of the Path, Withdrawer of the Directions, O Destroyer of the Kṣapa-rakṣasas;
O Foot, O Deity, O Fourfold One, O Seal of the Suras.
yakṣa-seal, rākṣasa-seal, vedī and vedimā;
Tape,
tattape, uṣṇāname,
prakhādya.
Nanava dhāraṇīya, aviśa diśāśodhane,
vākyaśuddhe jihvāśuddhe.
The purification of speech consists of wisdom, intelligence, mindfulness, discernment, understanding, steadfastness, calculation, and the wisdom of reliance;

through these points of resolute conviction regarding the wheel of victory and the wheel of emptiness—their cessation—fifty-six thousand asuras produced the thought of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and were established in the state of non-retrogression. (SjDh 15)
Thereupon, the Blessed One addressed the bodhisattva Vaiśāradyasamavasaraṇa:
"Noble son, the appearance of Tathāgatas in the world is rare;
rare, too, are these Drāviḍa mantra-words, which are permeated by ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation."
For the benefit of sentient beings and for the sake of accomplishing the qualities of a bodhisattva, noble son, when the Tathāgata was formerly practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva,
he embraced generosity, self-restraint, moderation, patience, vigor, meditative concentration, and wisdom; he attended upon many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas,
and in some instances, he gave gifts.
Virtue has been guarded, the holy life has been practiced, and in some respects, meditative cultivation has been pursued.
Patience has been cultivated, vigor has been exerted,
and concentration has been perfected.
Wisdom was cultivated,
and much immeasurable, diverse, and manifold kinds of wholesome karma were performed,
by which I have now attained unsurpassed knowledge.

For many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons, while formerly practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, the Tathāgata avoided false speech, slander, harsh words, and frivolous chatter; he cultivated and frequently practiced manifold kinds of wholesome vocal karma.
By which he has now obtained a broad tongue;
for indeed, noble son, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, do not speak otherwise.
Then the Blessed One performed a miraculous feat of supernatural power there.
Then, by means of that miraculous feat (*ṛddhy-abhisaṃskāra*), he entered the samādhi called "The Convergence of All Merit.
Extending his tongue from his mouth and covering his own face with it, sixty million rays of light were emitted from that tongue;
by them, this great trichiliocosm was filled with a magnificent radiance, such that the realms of hell, the animal realm, the world of Yama, the gods, and humans were all suffused.
And those rays [of light] caused cool breezes to blow for those hell-beings whose bodies were being consumed by blazing fire;
when they were touched by them, a pleasant sensation appeared for that moment.
And before each individual hell-being stood a manifestation of the Buddha, adorned with the thirty-two marks and the eighty secondary characteristics.
Upon seeing him, those inhabitants of hell were filled with happiness, their bodies nourished by the sight of the Buddha; and having seen the Buddha, they thought:
"By the power of this being, we have obtained pleasant sensations. They then conceived love, serene faith, and reverence toward the Blessed One.
The Buddha’s emanation said:
"O beings, speak thus!"
"Homage to the Buddha, homage to the Dharma, homage to the Saṅgha;
thus you shall always be endowed with happiness.
Then those beings in the hells, having raised their joined palms, uttered these words:

Homage to the Buddha, homage to the Dharma, homage to the Saṅgha! Then, by that root of merit from their mental clarity, those beings, having passed away from there, some were reborn among the gods and some among humans,
just as previously described, up to [the end].

Those beings in the cold hells, as well as *preta*s or *piśāca*s who were endowed with happiness, were reborn among gods and humans; thus the rays of light exhorted those in the worlds of gods, humans, and animals. Countless gods and humans approached the Blessed One, bowed their heads at his feet, and sat down to hear the Dharma of the Mahāyāna sūtra named *Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka*.
At that time, countless hosts of gods and humans conceived the aspiration for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
And here, bodhisattvas beyond counting have attained meditative concentrations, patient acceptances, and dhāraṇīs.
The Blessed One said this, and the entire assembly, including the world of gods, humans, asuras, garuḍas, and gandharvas, with joyful minds, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
[Page 21] Thus ends this *Sarvajñatākāradhāraṇī* in the noble Mahāyāna sūtra, the *Ārya-Śrīkaruṇāpuṇḍarīka*.
